title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper on a novel method related to lesion counting in medical imaging.

extractions.description: This paper presents a novel continuously differentiable function that maps lesion segmentation predictions to lesion count probability distributions in a consistent and robust manner. The proposed method is intended to augment lesion segmentation models with post hoc counting capabilities. It focuses on providing accurate and well-calibrated count distributions that can capture uncertainty information, and is demonstrated to be beneficial for multi-task learning, low data efficiency, and robustness against adversarial attacks.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is centered around a method for medical imaging concerning lesion counting, which does not directly impact climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Lesion counts are important indicators of disease severity, patient prognosis, and treatment efficacy, yet counting as a task in medical imaging is often overlooked in favor of segmentation.
